The 10 ms ticker of the observer frame is the measuring tool of the proof: what is judged is how many of its ticks ran inside the spin of the other frame, and the spins go on until one shows ticks (30 s), so a starved spin is a trial that proves nothing and never a red.

The spin of the other frame starts 50 ms after the call that asks for it has returned, so that call does not block on its own spin; the test then waits for the frame to say the spin is over, with a deadline of 30 s, and no verdict reads when the timer fired.

The 2 s tick is the model of a leak test's page and decides nothing: a srflx that comes after it is still read and posted, the status of the page is final (DONE or REFUSED) in the same step that says `posted`, and the verdict is read from the stamps of the gateway, the DoH and the TURN server, never from when the tick fired.

The 30 s of each channel are the deadline of its wait (`no answer` is a channel that stays silent). Every channel of a URL is asked at once and a name that is nowhere answers all of them, so on a healthy run no silence is waited for, and a stall of the machine cannot make one URL answer and the other not.

The timer of 30 s is the deadline of the wait for the end of the ICE gathering: the wait ends when the page says `complete`, a gathering that never completes returns what it has and fails the assertions on the candidates, and no verdict reads when the timer fired.

The 10 ms ticker of the top document is the measuring tool of the proof: strategy 1 needs ticks inside the spin of the iframe and the spins go on until one shows them (30 s); strategy 0 asserts there is none in any spin, which no machine can fake because one thread cannot tick while it spins.

The timer of 30 s ends a spin the iframe never reports (an empty trial that proves nothing, and the spins go on until one shows ticks or 30 s have passed); the spin ends the trial as soon as the iframe says so, with no further timer.

The server keeps the answer of the goto that must LAND for 1.5 s on purpose, so the goto is in flight while the old page acts; the verdict reads only a lower bound on how long the goto waited (a slow machine cannot make that red) and where the page ended.

The 50 ms poll only asks the server whether the request of the goto has arrived. For the cases that must be stopped the server keeps the goto's page until the test has seen the goto return, so a late poll lengthens the wait and cannot let the goto land (it ends at its timeout of 30 s); for the cases that must land, what the poll does changes where the goto ends and the assertions accept both.

The pause spaces the visits of a page the way the retail method does (visit, pause, visit); it is the minimum between two events the test generates, the UDP-free roads wait for the browser's own QUIC connection as a condition (30 s) before it, and the protocols the visits read do not depend on a longer pause.

The watcher of the page (an interval of 50 ms) is the measuring tool: it counts its own looks in window.__looks, and each test waits for the count to move past the call it checks, so no verdict is read before the watcher has looked at the page as the call left it.
The pause between two events the test generates is part of the stimulus; the assertion reads the events after every call has returned, not the time between them.
